title: Influence Bounded by Complementary Output Probability
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, let $J$ be a set of coordinates, and let $b\in\{-1,1\}$. The influence of $J$ toward $b$, defined as the fraction of inputs from which $J$ can make $f$ attain $b$ minus the fraction of inputs where $f$ already equals $b$, is at most one minus the fraction of inputs where $f$ equals $b$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$J$ is a finite set of coordinates among the $n$ coordinates
